title: Root Canal Treatment: What Really Happens in the Chair
excerpt: Root canal treatment has a scary reputation it no longer deserves. Here is a step-by-step look at what actually happens, how long it takes, and how to look after the tooth afterwards.
content:
Few dental words cause as much worry as root canal. Most of that fear comes from stories about treatment done decades ago. With modern anaesthesia, rotary instruments and digital X-rays, a root canal today feels very similar to getting a large filling.

Why would I need a root canal?

Inside every tooth is a soft core called the pulp, which contains nerves and blood vessels. When deep decay, a crack or repeated dental work lets bacteria reach the pulp, it becomes inflamed or infected. Common warning signs include:

  • Lingering pain with hot or cold drinks

  • Throbbing toothache that wakes you up at night

  • Swelling or a small pimple on the gum near the tooth

  • A tooth that has turned darker than its neighbours

The procedure, step by step

  1. Diagnosis: we take an IOPA X-ray and test the nerve to confirm the pulp cannot heal on its own.

  2. Anaesthesia: the area is numbed completely before we start.

  3. Cleaning and shaping: the infected pulp is removed and the canals are disinfected and shaped with fine instruments.

  4. Filling the canals: the clean canals are sealed with a rubber-like material called gutta-percha.

  5. Restoring the tooth: a filling and, for back teeth, a crown protects the tooth from fracture.

Most root canals are completed in two or three visits of 45 to 60 minutes each.

Root canal or extraction?

Root canal + crown

Extraction + implant

Keeps natural tooth

Yes

No

Typical visits

3 - 4

4 - 5 over 3 months

Approximate cost

₹10,000 - ₹18,000

₹35,000 - ₹45,000

Chewing feel

Natural

Very close to natural

Saving your own tooth is almost always the best option. Nothing we make in a lab bites quite like the tooth you were born with.

Aftercare tips

  • Avoid chewing hard food on the treated side until the crown is fitted

  • Take the prescribed medicines for the full course

  • Brush and floss normally - the tooth can still get decay at the margins

  • Come back for the crown on time; an uncrowned molar can crack

If you have a toothache that will not go away, book an appointment early. The sooner an infected tooth is treated, the simpler the treatment.

faqs.question: Is a root canal painful?
faqs.answer: No. The tooth is fully numbed, and most patients say it feels like a long filling. Mild soreness for a day or two afterwards is normal.

faqs.question: Do I really need a crown after a root canal?
faqs.answer: For molars and premolars, yes. A root-canal-treated back tooth becomes brittle and can split under chewing forces without a crown.

title: Dental Implants vs Bridges: Which Is Right for You?
excerpt: Missing a tooth? Implants and bridges both restore your smile, but they differ in cost, longevity and how they affect neighbouring teeth. Here is how to choose.
content:
Losing a tooth affects more than your smile. Neighbouring teeth slowly drift into the gap, the opposite tooth over-erupts and the jawbone in that area starts to shrink. Replacing the tooth early protects the rest of your mouth.

What is a dental implant?

An implant is a small titanium screw placed in the jawbone where the root used to be. After it fuses with the bone (usually 8 to 12 weeks), a crown is fixed on top. It stands on its own and does not need support from other teeth.

What is a bridge?

A bridge uses the teeth on either side of the gap as anchors. Those teeth are trimmed and capped, and a false tooth is suspended between them. It is fixed in about two visits.

Side-by-side comparison

Factor

Implant

Bridge

Treatment time

3 - 4 months

1 - 2 weeks

Neighbouring teeth

Untouched

Trimmed for crowns

Expected life

20+ years with care

10 - 15 years

Bone preservation

Yes

No

Cost (single tooth)

₹30,000 - ₹45,000

₹15,000 - ₹20,000

Who is a good candidate for implants?

  • Adults with healthy gums and enough bone (checked with a CBCT scan)

  • Non-smokers, or smokers willing to stop during healing

  • Patients with controlled diabetes

If the teeth next to the gap are healthy and untouched, an implant lets you replace the missing tooth without drilling into good teeth.

Both options work well when planned properly. During your consultation we will look at your X-rays, bone levels and budget and recommend what will last longest for you.

title: 7 Daily Habits for Healthier Gums
excerpt: Bleeding gums are not normal. These seven simple habits take a few minutes a day and can stop gum disease before it starts.
content:
Gum disease is the most common reason adults lose teeth, yet it is almost entirely preventable. The early stage, gingivitis, is fully reversible - if you catch it in time.

The 7 habits

  1. Brush twice for two minutes with a soft brush, angled at 45 degrees towards the gumline.

  2. Clean between teeth daily with floss or interdental brushes - a brush alone misses about a third of the tooth surface.

  3. Do not skip the night brush. Saliva flow drops during sleep, so bacteria do more damage overnight.

  4. Use fluoride toothpaste and spit, do not rinse, so the fluoride stays on your teeth.

  5. Cut down on sugary snacks between meals, especially sticky sweets and packaged juices.

  6. Stop smoking and gutkha. Tobacco hides gum bleeding while the disease silently gets worse.

  7. Get a professional cleaning every six months to remove hardened tartar you cannot brush away.

Warning signs to watch for

  • Gums that bleed while brushing or flossing

  • Bad breath that does not go away

  • Gums pulling away from the teeth

  • Teeth that feel loose or have started to shift

Healthy gums do not bleed. If yours do, that is your body asking for help - not a reason to brush less.

If you notice any of these signs, a simple scaling and polishing session is often all it takes to get your gums back on track.

faqs.question: Should I stop brushing if my gums bleed?
faqs.answer: No. Keep brushing gently. Bleeding usually reduces within a week of good cleaning; if it does not, see a dentist.

faqs.question: How often do I need scaling?
faqs.answer: For most people every six months. Smokers, diabetics and people with braces may need it every three to four months.

title: Clear Aligners for Adults: A Complete Guide
excerpt: Straight teeth without metal brackets. Here is how clear aligners work, how long treatment takes, what it costs, and the habits that make treatment succeed.
content:
More adults than ever are straightening their teeth, and clear aligners are a big reason why. They are nearly invisible, removable and comfortable - but they only work if you wear them properly.

How do aligners work?

After a digital scan, a series of custom trays is made. Each tray moves your teeth a fraction of a millimetre. You switch to a new tray every one to two weeks, and the teeth gradually move into place.

Who can get aligners?

  • Mild to moderate crowding

  • Gaps between teeth

  • Some bite problems such as overbite and crossbite

  • Relapse after braces in childhood

What a typical journey looks like

  1. Consultation, OPG and digital scan

  2. Treatment plan with a 3D preview of your final smile

  3. Attachments placed and first trays fitted

  4. Reviews every 3 to 6 weeks

  5. Retainers once the teeth are in position

Aligners move teeth only while they are in your mouth. Twenty-two hours a day is not a suggestion - it is the treatment.

Tips for success

  • Remove trays to eat and drink anything other than water

  • Brush before putting the trays back in

  • Keep the case with you - most lost trays are wrapped in a tissue

  • Wear your retainers as advised after treatment

Treatment typically takes 9 to 15 months. At your consultation we can tell you whether aligners or fixed braces will give you the better result.

title: Your Child's First Dental Visit: A Parent's Checklist
excerpt: The first dental visit should happen by your child's first birthday. Here is how to prepare, what we check, and how to make it a positive experience.
content:
Milk teeth may fall out eventually, but they hold space for permanent teeth, help children chew and speak clearly, and decay in them can be painful. Starting dental visits early makes them routine instead of scary.

When should the first visit be?

Ideally within six months of the first tooth appearing, and no later than the first birthday.

Before the visit

  • Book a morning slot when your child is fresh

  • Talk about the dentist positively - avoid words like 'hurt' or 'injection'

  • Bring a favourite toy for comfort

  • Note any habits such as thumb sucking or bottle feeding at night

What happens during the check-up

  1. A gentle look at teeth, gums and bite - often on the parent's lap

  2. Advice on brushing technique and the right amount of toothpaste

  3. Fluoride application if needed

  4. A plan for the next visit, usually every six months

A child who has only ever had happy dental visits grows into an adult who is not afraid of the dentist.

Sealants and fluoride are simple, painless ways to prevent cavities in children. Ask us about them at your next visit.

faqs.answer: A smear the size of a grain of rice until age three, then a pea-sized amount.

faqs.answer: It is normal in infants, but if it continues beyond four or five years it can affect the bite. We can suggest gentle ways to stop the habit.

title: Wisdom Teeth Removal: Recovery Tips That Actually Help
excerpt: Most people are back to normal within a week of wisdom tooth surgery. These practical tips help you heal faster and avoid a painful dry socket.
content:
Wisdom teeth usually appear between 17 and 25 years of age. When there is not enough room, they get stuck (impacted) and can cause pain, swelling and decay in the tooth in front.

The first 24 hours

  • Bite on the gauze for 45 minutes after surgery

  • Use an ice pack on the cheek - 10 minutes on, 10 minutes off

  • Eat cold, soft food like curd, kheer or ice cream

  • Do not spit, rinse forcefully or drink through a straw

Days 2 to 7

  1. Start warm salt-water rinses after meals

  2. Take painkillers on time, not after the pain becomes severe

  3. Brush the other teeth gently; clean near the wound carefully

  4. Return for suture removal or review after a week

The blood clot in the socket is your natural bandage. Everything you do in the first two days is about protecting it.

When to call us

  • Pain that increases after the third day

  • Swelling that keeps growing after 48 hours

  • Fever or a bad taste from the socket

  • Bleeding that does not stop with firm pressure

With the right care, wisdom tooth removal is a routine procedure and most patients return to work in two to three days.

faqs.question: What is a dry socket?
faqs.answer: It happens when the blood clot is dislodged, exposing the bone. It causes throbbing pain around day three and is easily treated with a medicated dressing.

faqs.question: Do all wisdom teeth need removal?
faqs.answer: No. Fully erupted, healthy wisdom teeth that you can clean well can stay. We advise removal only when they cause problems.

title: How Laser Dentistry Makes Treatment More Comfortable
excerpt: Lasers let us treat gums and soft tissue with less bleeding, fewer stitches and faster healing. Here is where they help most.
content:
A dental laser is a precise beam of light that can cut, shape or disinfect soft tissue. Because it seals blood vessels as it works, there is very little bleeding and usually no need for stitches.

Where lasers help

  • Gum depigmentation - lightening dark gums for a more even smile

  • Gum contouring - correcting a 'gummy' smile

  • Mouth ulcers - quick pain relief and faster healing

  • Gum disease - disinfecting deep pockets alongside cleaning

Benefits for patients

  1. Less need for injections in many procedures

  2. Minimal bleeding and swelling

  3. Faster healing with lower infection risk

  4. Shorter appointments

For many of our anxious patients, the laser is the difference between avoiding treatment and actually getting it done.

Lasers are not a replacement for every instrument, but where they fit, they make dental care noticeably more comfortable.

title: From Hiding My Smile to Loving It: A Patient Story
excerpt: A college student who stopped smiling in photos because of a gap and a chipped front tooth shares how a single bonding appointment changed that.
content:
Shared with the patient's permission. Name changed for privacy.

Meera, a 21-year-old college student from Sonipat, had a small gap between her front teeth and a chipped edge from a fall in school. "I had mastered the closed-mouth smile," she told us. "In every group photo I was the one not showing teeth."

The consultation

She expected to be told she needed braces or veneers. After examining her teeth, we suggested composite bonding: a tooth-coloured material sculpted directly onto the teeth, with no drilling and no injections.

Treatment day

  1. Shade matched to her natural teeth

  2. Gap closed and chipped edge rebuilt in layers

  3. Shaped and polished to a natural shine

The whole appointment took about an hour and a half.

I kept checking the mirror in the auto on the way home. I had not smiled like that since school.

Looking after bonding

  • Avoid biting directly into very hard food with the front teeth

  • Limit tea and coffee in the first 48 hours

  • Get the bonding polished at routine check-ups

Not every smile needs an expensive makeover. Sometimes a small, conservative change makes the biggest difference.

title: Teeth Whitening Myths You Should Stop Believing
excerpt: Charcoal powder, lemon and baking soda are all over social media. Here is what actually whitens teeth safely - and what damages them.
content:
Draft - to be reviewed by Dr. Kavita before publishing.

Myth 1: Charcoal toothpaste whitens teeth

Charcoal mostly scrubs off surface stains and can wear down enamel over time, making teeth look more yellow in the long run.

Myth 2: Whitening damages enamel

Professional whitening gels used under supervision do not damage enamel. Temporary sensitivity is common and settles within a few days.

  • Lemon and baking soda - acidic and abrasive, avoid

  • Whitening strips - mild results, follow instructions

  • In-office whitening - fastest, most predictable results

If it fizzes, burns or scratches, it does not belong on your teeth.

title: Crowns and Bridges: How Long Do They Last?
excerpt: A well-made crown can last 15 years or more. Here is what affects its lifespan and how to make yours last.
content:
Crowns and bridges are among the most durable dental restorations, but they are not maintenance-free.

Materials compared

  • PFM (porcelain fused to metal) - strong and economical

  • Zirconia - very strong, metal-free, good for back teeth

  • E-max - the most natural look for front teeth

What shortens a crown's life

  1. Decay at the edge of the crown

  2. Grinding and clenching at night

  3. Using teeth to open packets or bottles
